The '''1997–98 season''' was the [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|96th season]] in [[Real Madrid CF]]'s history and their 67th consecutive season in [[La Liga]].

Real Madrid failed to retain their La Liga title, but made up for the domestic disappointment by winning the [[1997–98 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] with a 1–0 victory over [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[1998 UEFA Champions League Final|Amsterdam final]]. The European Cup title was Real Madrid's 7th overall and first since [[1966 European Cup Final|1966]]. This, however, was not enough to save the job of manager [[Jupp Heynckes]], who was sacked due to Madrid's low [[1997–98 La Liga|league]] finish just eight days after the European triumph. In the [[1997–98 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], Real lost to [[Deportivo Alavés|Alaves]] in the round of 16 on away goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/heynckes-couldnt-work-with-sons-of-bitches-at-real-madrid/1uy31rr4svtjk1qlum6kuwl99c|title=Heynckes Couldn't work with sons of b*s at Real Madrid|publisher=goal.com|date=24 February 2019|access-date=2 July 2020}}</ref>

==Kit==
Real Madrid's kits were manufactured by Spanish apparel manufacturer [[Kelme (company)|Kelme]] and sponsored by Teka.
